preheader: OpenAI's revenue reality check, Ray Dalio's bubble warning, and a potential Starbucks-Chipotle tie-up.

lead.headline: OpenAI's Annualized Revenue Reportedly $20 Billion Lower Than Expected
lead.body: OpenAI's actual annualized revenue is $50 billion, which is significantly lower than the $70 billion previously reported to investors. The discrepancy comes down to how different AI companies account for revenue generated through cloud partner sales.
lead.why: As a business student interested in investing, this is a prime example of why you must look past startup hype and understand the accounting rules that companies use to report their sales.

stories.headline: Ray Dalio Warns the AI Bubble Is Nearing Its Bursting Point
stories.body: Billionaire investor Ray Dalio warned that rising interest rates, heavy borrowing for AI, and pressure to turn paper wealth into cash are pushing the market toward a bubble burst.
stories.why: If you are building a personal investment portfolio, Dalio's warning is a reminder to focus on companies with strong cash flows rather than pure market hype.

stories.headline: Starbucks Explored a Potential Takeover of Chipotle
stories.body: Starbucks confirmed it is focusing on its turnaround plan following reports that it explored a potential merger with Chipotle. The deal would have reunited Starbucks CEO Brian Niccol with his former company.
stories.why: This shows how corporate strategy and leadership transitions can spark massive merger rumors, which is a core topic in consulting and corporate finance.

stories.headline: Nvidia-Backed Lumentum Sold Out of AI Server Parts Until 2029
stories.body: Optical component maker Lumentum is completely sold out of its advanced indium phosphide devices through early 2029. The company is currently unable to meet about 70% of the demand from tech firms building faster AI data centers.
stories.why: This highlights the massive hardware bottlenecks in the AI boom, offering a clear target for tech and infrastructure investors.

stories.headline: Apple Reportedly Set to Debut Touchscreen MacBook Pro This Month
stories.body: Apple plans to unveil its first touchscreen MacBook Pro and an updated iPad Mini on or around October 27. This comes just weeks after another rumored Apple event on October 13.
stories.why: Keeping track of Apple's hardware roadmap helps you understand consumer tech trends and product strategy.

stories.headline: Deloitte Fined £6 Million Over 'Concerning' Audit Failures
stories.body: The UK's Financial Reporting Council fined Deloitte over £6 million for its audits of transport firm Go-Ahead. The watchdog cited a highly concerning pattern of failure spanning a five-year period.
stories.why: If you are eyeing a career in consulting or accounting at a Big Four firm, this highlights the intense regulatory scrutiny and risk management these firms face.

stories.headline: AI Reshapes the Job Market as Entry-Level Postings Decline
stories.body: Former AI lead at Salesforce and Meta, Clara Shih, noted that companies have slowed down entry-level hiring as AI automates routine tasks. This shift is leading to a decline in junior job postings in major hubs like New York City.
stories.why: As a first-year business student, you need to focus early on building strategic, specialized skills rather than relying on routine tasks to secure your first internship.

stories.headline: Tragedy at UC Irvine as First-Year Student Passes Away in Dorm
stories.body: Amir Eftekhar, an 18-year-old student, was tragically found dead in his Orange County dorm room over the weekend. The Orange County Coroner confirmed the death was a suicide.

stories.headline: Alex Eala Avoids WTA Sanctions Ahead of Wuhan Open
stories.body: Filipina tennis player Alex Eala received good news that she will not face WTA sanctions for skipping the mandatory China Open to represent her country in the Asian Games.

term.name: GAAP (Generally Accepted Accounting Principles)
term.definition: GAAP is a standardized set of accounting rules and procedures used by companies to compile their financial statements. Today's news shows how GAAP-compliant companies like OpenAI and Anthropic can report vastly different revenue figures based on how they choose to record partner sales.

serve.headline: VEIR raised $110M to swap copper for superconductors in AI data centers
serve.body: VEIR makes superconducting power cables designed to deliver electricity to power-hungry AI data centers. The oversubscribed Series C round was co-led by Matter Venture Partners and Tyche Partners.
